result.title: When Chekhov's Gun Fires Anyway: Over-Realization in Text-to-Image Models
result.summary: In text-to-image generation, a target that the prompt mentions often appears in the generated image in a way the prompt does not call for. We call this failure over-realization. Mental-spaces theory points to the situations where it can happen: under a negation, inside what a character believes or imagines, as the vehicle of a figurative comparison, or behind a viewpoint that hides the target. Prior work has studied only negation in depth, and the conventional alignment and preference metrics do not penalize the failure. We build OverReal to measure it: OverReal-Gen, 698 prompts covering the four situations, on which we measure each generator's over-realization rate; and OverReal-Det, 2,841 generated images human-labeled for whether and how the target is over-realized, on which we verify the automatic judge that produces this rate. Our evaluation of eight text-to-image systems reveals that all of them over-realize, and that conventional metrics such as CLIPScore reward the failure rather than penalize it. Prompt expansion only partly mitigates the failure. Inside the generator, the diffusion backbone attends to a mentioned target almost as much as to a requested one. The cue words that should hold the target back receive less attention than ordinary words.

AI.brief_summary: 论文定义 text-to-image 中的「over-realization」失败：提示只提及、并未要求的目标仍出现在生成图中，涉及否定、角色信念/想象、比喻载体与被视角遮挡四种情境；作者构建 OverReal-Gen 提示集与 OverReal-Det 人工标注图集，评测八个生成系统，发现均存在该问题，且 CLIPScore 等常规指标反而奖励它。
AI.relevance_reason: 其内部分析显示扩散主干对「仅被提及」目标的注意力接近「被请求」目标、而约束性 cue 词注意力偏低，这一「提及 vs 任务必需」的表示区分与指标设计可能可供核查 VLM 是否在内部保留否定、假设等任务必要信息；但论文属图像生成任务，与 LVR 推理状态生成无直接关联。
